tom: Ran a focused sanity sweep this morning across A100/H100/L40S — wanted to capture behavior when we toggle between fused-paged flash variants + our new batcher heuristic. Short summary up front: H100 shows a ~12% regression for fused-paged at seq=2048, bsz=4 vs previous baseline; A100/L40S look stable. Details below.

ainna: thanks — can you paste the exact config and the run artifacts?

tom: sure. command used: `./bench/attn_sweep --gpus A100,H100,L40S --variants fused,paged,flashmix --seqs 128,512,1024,2048 --bsz 1,2,4,8 --kvcache on --warmups 10 --iters 200`

tom: attaching top-lines from the CSV (columns: gpu,variant,seq,bsz,median_p95_ms,median_mean_ms):
```
A100,fused,2048,4,18.2,12.7
H100,fused,2048,4,21.0,14.2
L40S,fused,2048,4,19.1,13.0
H100,paged,2048,4,18.0,12.5
H100,flashmix,2048,4,17.8,12.3
```

rajiv: interesting — H100 fused path is the outlier here. Do we know if kernel selector picked a different kernel rollout compared to baseline?

tom: kernel selector logs show the same picked kernel ID (k_fused_v3) but the runtime emitted fallback traces to k_vectorized on ~8% of requests during the same run. I think we had a micro-regression that causes occasional fallback. Logs: `selector: chosen k_fused_v3; fallback_count=16/200; fallback_to=k_vectorized`

marie: fallback -> that often explains the p95 bump. Did the fallback correlate with spikes in occupancy or memory fragmentation (KV cache spills)?

tom: I checked memory traces. KV cache hit-rate stayed ~99.6% but we saw 2x more small memcpy ops in H100 fused run vs paged. Stack traces point to an extra memcpy around `kv_write_back` when prefetched pages are being stitched.

ainna: can you share perf counters? SM utilization / L2 bandwidth / pcie stalls for H100 fused 2048/4?

tom: pasted snapshot: `SM:78%, L2_bandwidth:520GB/s, memcpy_small_ops: 182, pcie_wait: 2%`. For A100 fused 2048/4: `SM:81%, L2:490GB/s, memcpy_small_ops: 21, pcie_wait: 1%`

perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood.example/runs/3280123456/artifact.tar.gz (contains nvprof traces, kernel timelines, selector logs) :robot_face:

rajiv: thanks. Two hypotheses: 1) new fused kernel's shared-mem tiling on H100 is triggering extra memcpy path for kv page stitching; 2) scheduling jitter on H100 when swapping between fused/paged code paths causes short-lived spills. We should reproduce with microbench that isolates kv_write_back.

tom: agree. I already started a micro-run that toggles only `KV_PREFETCH=on/off` and runs `kv_write_back` hotspot 1e6 times on H100 to measure memcpy overhead. ETA 30m.

marie: also try disabling the selector and forcing k_fused_v2 vs k_fused_v3, to see if it regresses on a per-kernel basis. If k_v2 is ok then revert selector mapping for H100 temporarily.

tom: good call. I'll run three microbench variants: (A) forced k_fused_v2, (B) forced k_fused_v3, (C) selector on (baseline). Will post numbers.

ainna: if it's kernel-specific we should plan a canary change: remap H100 default to k_fused_v2 and schedule a gated test for 24h. Capture p95 and error rates.

tom: microbench results (H100, seq=2048, bsz=4, kv_prefetch toggle):
```
forced_k_fused_v2,kv_prefetch_on,median_p95_ms=16.9,memcpy_small_ops=24
forced_k_fused_v3,kv_prefetch_on,median_p95_ms=20.9,memcpy_small_ops=178
selector_on,kv_prefetch_on,median_p95_ms=21.1,memcpy_small_ops=182
forced_k_fused_v3,kv_prefetch_off,median_p95_ms=18.1,memcpy_small_ops=9
```

rajiv: that pretty clearly points to an interaction between k_fused_v3 and kv_prefetch path on H100. With kv_prefetch off v3 behaves reasonable.

marie: what's the code path difference between v2 and v3 w.r.t. prefetch? I thought v3 added speculative prefetch and page stitching to reduce cold starts.

tom: correct — v3's tiled prefetch uses an asynchronous stitching routine that ends up calling a small memcpy for each stitched chunk; on H100 the memcpy appears to contend with the kernel's writeback path causing stalls. Hypothesis: on H100 the small memcpy isn't coalesced and hits L2 thrash.

ainna: mitigations? We can either: A) revert H100 default to v2, B) patch v3 to batch memcpy into bigger coalesced ops, or C) change selector to prefer paged/flashmix for seq>=2048 and bsz<=4.

rajiv: I'd prefer B long-term; short-term do A + C as a safety net. Patch and canary plan: remap H100->k_fused_v2 for the next release, and add selector rule: if seq>=1024 && bsz<=4 => prefer paged/flashmix on H100.

tom: I'll open the PR with the selector rule and the emergency remap. PR will include a note linking perf artifacts and microbench results.

perf-bot: PR created: https://git.redwood.example/r/infra/selector-config/+/3257 (includes test matrix) :white_check_mark:

marie: thanks. once PR is staged, let's run canary across our dedicated pool (5 machines H100) for 12h and watch p95 + tail latency traces. If green we keep. If not, rollback.

tom: scheduled canary job: `canary-run --pool=dedicated-h100-small --duration=12h --variant=remap-kfusedv2` (job id: canary-3280123499)

ainna: great. also add a ticket for v3 memcpy coalescing with priority P1.

tom: created ticket INF-8672 (P1) — title: "Coalesce v3 stitched memcpy to avoid L2 thrash on H100".

rajiv: good summary. add this thread to the perf retro doc and mark followups.

tom: will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
